arxiv-2101-10803.title: ACAV100M: Automatic Curation of Large-Scale Datasets for Audio-Visual Video Representation Learning
arxiv-2101-10803.creator: Sangho Lee, Jiwan Chung, Youngjae Yu, Gunhee Kim, Thomas Breuel, Gal Chechik, Yale Song, https://acav100m.github.io
arxiv-2101-10803.description: Abstract The natural association between visual observations and their corresponding sound provides powerful self-supervisory signals for learning video representations, which makes the ever-growing amount of online videos an attractive source of training data. However, large portions of online videos contain irrelevant audio-visual signals because of edited/overdubbed audio, and models trained on such uncurated videos have shown to learn suboptimal representations.

arxiv-2102-12486.title: OH Megamasers in H I Surveys: Forecasts and a Machine Learning Approach to Separating Disks from Mergers Astropy ( Robitaille et al. 2013 ) , Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , Numpy ( Van Der Walt et al. 2011 ) , Scipy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 ) , Scikit-Learn ( Pedregosa et al. 2011 ) , MAGPHYS ( Da Cunha
arxiv-2102-12486.creator: Hayley Roberts, Jeremy Darling, Andrew J. Baker
arxiv-2102-12486.description: Abstract OH megamasers (OHMs) are rare, luminous masers found in gas-rich major galaxy mergers. In untargeted neutral hydrogen ( H I ) emission-line surveys, spectroscopic redshifts are necessary to differentiate the λ rest = 18 \lambda_{\text{rest}}=18 cm masing lines produced by OHMs from H I 21 cm lines.

arxiv-2302-14389.title: Information-Restricted Neural Language Models Reveal Different Brain Regions’ Sensitivity to Semantics, Syntax and Context
arxiv-2302-14389.creator: Alexandre Pasquiou, Yair Lakretz, Bertrand Thirion, Christophe Pallier
arxiv-2302-14389.description: Abstract A fundamental question in neurolinguistics concerns the brain regions involved in syntactic and semantic processing during speech comprehension, both at the lexical (word processing) and supra-lexical levels (sentence and discourse processing). To what extent are these regions separated or intertwined?

arxiv-2308-06898.title: CupCleaner: A Data Cleaning Approach for Comment Updating
arxiv-2308-06898.creator: Qingyuan Liang, Zeyu Sun, Qihao Zhu, Junhao Hu, Yifan Zhao, Lu Zhang
arxiv-2308-06898.description: Abstract Recently, deep learning-based techniques have shown promising performance on various tasks related to software engineering. For these learning-based approaches to perform well, obtaining high-quality data is one fundamental and crucial issue. The comment updating task is an emerging software engineering task aiming at automatically updating the corresponding comments based on changes in source code.

arxiv-2402-02486.title: Spatial resolution effects on the solar open flux estimates
arxiv-2402-02486.creator: I. Milić, R. Centeno, X. Sun, M. Rempel J. de la Cruz Rodríguez
arxiv-2402-02486.description: Abstract Context. Spectropolarimetric observations used to infer the solar magnetic fields are obtained with a limited spatial resolution. The effects of this limited resolution on the inference of the open flux over the observed region have not been extensively studied. Aims.

arxiv-2406-00062.title: Unlocking the Potential of Large Language Models for Clinical Text Anonymization: A Comparative Study
arxiv-2406-00062.creator: David Pissarra, Isabel Curioso, João Alveira, Duarte Pereira, Bruno Ribeiro
arxiv-2406-00062.description: Abstract Automated clinical text anonymization has the potential to unlock the widespread sharing of textual health data for secondary usage while assuring patient privacy and safety. Despite the proposal of many complex and theoretically successful anonymization solutions in literature, these techniques remain flawed. As such, clinical institutions are still reluctant to apply them for open access to their data.

arxiv-2406-14157.title: Exact solutions for differentially rotating galaxies in general relativity
arxiv-2406-14157.creator: Marco Galoppo, David L. Wiltshire
arxiv-2406-14157.description: Abstract Two classes of stationary axisymmetric solutions of Einstein’s equations for isolated differentially rotating matter sources are presented. The asymptotic regime is extracted, with attention to quasilocal gravitational energy, shear and angular momentum related by the Raychaudhuri equation. At outer boundaries the quasilocal angular momentum and energy densities vanish, defining novel geometric structures – the vortex surface and the rotosurface.

arxiv-2407-06717.title: Acoustic axes conditions revised
arxiv-2407-06717.creator: Yakov Itin
arxiv-2407-06717.description: Abstract The explanation of the basic acoustic properties of crystals requires a recognition of the acoustic axes. To derive the acoustic axes in a given material, one requires both a workable method and the necessary and sufficient criteria for the existence of the acoustic axes in a partial propagation direction.

arxiv-2408-09225.title: Explicit Constructions for Poncelet Polygons
arxiv-2408-09225.creator: Leah Wrenn Berman, Gábor Gévay
arxiv-2408-09225.description: Abstract We study the geometric structure of Poncelet n n -gons from a projective point of view. In particular we present explicit constructions of Poncelet n n -gons for certain n n and derive algebraic characterisations in terms of bracket polynomials.

arxiv-2411-17804.title: Comparison of Fast, Hybrid Imaging Architectures for Multi-scale, Hierarchical Aperture Arrays
arxiv-2411-17804.creator: Nithyanandan Thyagarajan
arxiv-2411-17804.description: Abstract Two major areas of modern radio astronomy, namely, explosive astrophysical transient phenomena and observations of cosmological structures, are driving the design of aperture arrays towards large numbers of low-cost elements consisting of multiple spatial scales spanning the dimensions of individual elements, the size of stations (groupings of individual elements), and the spacing between stations.

arxiv-2503-11600.title: Supervised Distributed Computing Thanks: John Augustine is supported by the Centre for Cybersecurity, Trust and Reliability (CyStar), IIT Madras. Christian Scheideler and Julian Werthmann are funded by the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, German Research Foundation) – 549499840.
arxiv-2503-11600.creator: John Augustine, Christian Scheideler, Julian Werthmann
arxiv-2503-11600.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by John Augustine, Christian Scheideler, Julian Werthmann. We introduce a new framework for distributed computing that extends and refines the standard master-worker approach of scheduling multi-threaded computations. In this framework, there are different roles: a supervisor, a source, a target, and a collection of workers. Initially, the source stores some instance I I of a computational problem, and at the end, the target is supposed to store a correct solution S ⁡ ( I ) S(I) for that instance.

arxiv-2504-18226.title: Phenomenology of Schwarzschild-like Black Holes with a Generalized Compton Wavelength
arxiv-2504-18226.creator: Reggie C. Pantig, Ali Övgün, Gaetano Lambiase
arxiv-2504-18226.description: Abstract We investigate the influence of the generalized Compton wavelength (GCW), emerging from a three-dimensional dynamical quantum vacuum (3D DQV) on Schwarzschild-like black hole spacetimes, motivated by the work of Fiscaletti [10.1134/S0040577925020096] Fiscaletti 2025 . The GCW modifies the classical geometry through a deformation parameter ε \varepsilon , encoding quantum gravitational backreaction.

arxiv-2510-16083.title: PassREfinder-FL : Privacy-Preserving Credential Stuffing Risk Prediction via Graph-Based Federated Learning for Representing Password Reuse between Websites
arxiv-2510-16083.creator: Jaehan Kim, Minkyoo Song, Minjae Seo, Youngjin Jin, Seungwon Shin, Jinwoo Kim
arxiv-2510-16083.description: Abstract Credential stuffing attacks have caused significant harm to online users who frequently reuse passwords across multiple websites. While prior research has attempted to detect users with reused passwords or identify malicious login attempts, existing methods often compromise usability by restricting password creation or website access, and their reliance on complex account-sharing mechanisms hinders real-world deployment.

arxiv-2512-01845.title: JPEGs Just Got Snipped: Croppable Signatures Against Deepfake Images
arxiv-2512-01845.creator: 1 st Pericle Perazzo, 2 nd Massimiliano Mattei, 3 rd Giuseppe Anastasi, 4 th Marco Avvenuti, 5 th Gianluca Dini, 6 th Giuseppe Lettieri, 7 th Carlo Vallati
arxiv-2512-01845.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by 1 st Pericle Perazzo, 2 nd Massimiliano Mattei, 3 rd Giuseppe Anastasi, 4 th Marco Avvenuti, 5 th Gianluca Dini, 6 th Giuseppe Lettieri, 7 th Carlo Vallati. Deepfakes are a type of synthetic media created using artificial intelligence, specifically deep learning algorithms. This technology can for example superimpose faces and voices onto videos, creating hyper-realistic but artificial representations.

arxiv-2602-03238.title: The Necessity of a Unified Framework for LLM-Based Agent Evaluation
arxiv-2602-03238.creator: Pengyu Zhu, Li Sun, Philip S. Yu, Sen Su
arxiv-2602-03238.description: Abstract With the advent of Large Language Models (LLMs), general-purpose agents have seen fundamental advancements. However, evaluating these agents presents unique challenges that distinguish them from static QA benchmarks. We observe that current agent benchmarks are heavily confounded by extraneous factors, including system prompts, toolset configurations, and environmental dynamics.

pmc-10532112.creator: Sadia Tareq, Edward Tranah, Kevin Tsoi
pmc-10532112.description: IntroductionKnowing when to screen for malignancy is an important aspect of care within rheumatology. We herein present the case of a patient with rheumatoid arthritis who developed painful and circumferential swelling in both lower limbs which rapidly progressed to involve her arms, trunk and abdomen, following a third cycle of rituximab.

pmc-11359800.title: The Silent Syndrome of Long COVID and Gaps in Scientific Knowledge: A Narrative Review
pmc-11359800.creator: Rosilene da Silva, Antonio Carlos Rosário Vallinoto, Eduardo José Melo dos Santos
pmc-11359800.description: COVID-19 is still a major public health concern, mainly due to the persistence of symptoms or the appearance of new symptoms. To date, more than 200 symptoms of long COVID (LC) have been described. The present review describes and maps its relevant clinical characteristics, pathophysiology, epidemiology, and genetic and nongenetic risk factors.

pmc-11674709.title: Nanolabels Prepared by the Entrapment or Self-Assembly of Signaling Molecules for Colorimetric and Fluorescent Immunoassays
pmc-11674709.creator: Ning Xia, Yadi Li, Cancan He, Dehua Deng
pmc-11674709.description: Nanomaterials have attracted significant attention as signal reporters for immunoassays. They can directly generate detectable signals or release a large number of signaling elements for readout. Among various nanolabels, nanomaterials composed of multiple signaling molecules have shown great potential in immunoassays. Generally, signaling molecules can be entrapped in nanocontainers or self-assemble into nanostructures for signal amplification.

pmc-12532419.title: Correlation between serum AMH, AFC, AND histologically quantified primordial follicles: a prospective study in premenopausal women

pmc-12532419.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the relationship between serum Anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) levels, antral follicle count (AFC), and histologically quantified primordial follicle numbers in premenopausal women, in order to validate the clinical accuracy of AMH and AFC as surrogate markers of true ovarian reserve.

pmc-12651435.title: Blood–brain barrier opening as a predictor of epilepsy and mortality after subarachnoid haemorrhage
pmc-12651435.creator: Jens P Dreier, Svetlana Lublinsky, Viktor Horst, Sebastian Major, Coline L Lemale, Vasilis Kola, Maren KL Winkler, Eun-Jeung Kang, Karl Schoknecht, Nils Hecht, Anna Maslarova, Edgar Santos, Johannes Platz, Christina M Kowoll, Oliver W Sakowitz, Erdem Güresir, Hartmut Vatter, Christian Dohmen, Stefan
pmc-12651435.description: SummaryBackgroundWe determined the predictive power of semi-automated blood–brain barrier assessment and other variables collected during neurocritical care for the outcome of ‘epilepsy or late death’ following aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage.MethodsThis is a secondary analysis of the prospective, non-interventional, prognostic DISCHARGE-1-cohort from six university hospitals in Germany. All patients who underwent at least one contrast-enhanced MRI during neurocritical care were included.

pmc-12654726.title: EVD-Associated Infections in Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: Risk Factors and Clinical Predictions—A Retrospective Single-Center Study
pmc-12654726.creator: Hraq Sarkis, Abed Alrazzak Kerhani, Ann-Kathrin Joerger, Carolin Albrecht, Chiara Negwer, Maria Wostrack, Arthur Wagner, Bernhard Meyer, Allison B Reiss
pmc-12654726.description: Background and Objectives: External ventricular drain (EVD)-associated infections are a serious complication in subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) patients, with reported incidence rates of 1–45%. Existing prediction models show limited performance and focus on the static risk factors assessed at insertion, failing to examine how infection risk changes over time.

pmc-13050574.title: Management of Symptomatic and Asymptomatic May-Thurner Syndrome: A Review of Two Cases
pmc-13050574.creator: Luis A Cruz Vásquez, Manuela Restrepo Gomez, Oscar F Vargas, Luis F Rivera
pmc-13050574.description: May-Thurner syndrome is a condition in which there is obstruction of blood flow in the left iliac vein due to compression between the right iliac artery and the spine. We present two clinical cases of women with venous compressive May-Thurner syndrome who underwent endovascular management with the insertion of a dedicated venous stent.

pmc-13229914.title: Perforated acalculous cholecystitis in a neutropenic patient following chemotherapy: a fatal case report
pmc-13229914.creator: Yunpeng (Jack) Deng
pmc-13229914.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Acalculous cholecystitis is an uncommon but serious complication of myelosuppressive chemotherapy that is most often observed during profound neutropenia and carries a substantially high morbidity and mortality. This case describes the fulminant course of acalculous cholecystitis in a 78-year-old female receiving carboplatin and vinorelbine for non-small cell lung cancer, with rapid progression from initial presentation to septic shock and multiorgan failure.

pmc-13331729.title: Mixed-methods characterization of the tasks and factors influencing occupational exposure during biosolids land application
pmc-13331729.creator: Riley J. L. Demo, Carsten Prasse, Keeve E. Nachman, Sara N. Lupolt
pmc-13331729.description: BackgroundPathogenic and chemical contaminants in biosolids may pose risks to workers during land application. Characterizing biosolids applicators’ exposures and risks requires information about the tasks and processes involved in the transportation, application, and use of biosolids, which is critically lacking.

pmc-13349999.title: Predicting adherence of imatinib in gastrointestinal stromal tumor—rise of the machines!
pmc-13349999.creator: Thiru Prasanna, Desmond Yip

pmc-13388000.title: Shotgun Metagenomic Profiling of the Gut Virome in Prodromal and Confirmed Parkinson's Disease
pmc-13388000.creator: Deepika Dinesh, Xochitl C Morgan, Jordan Jensen, Kjetil Bjornevik, Michael A Schwarzschild, Alberto Ascherio, Curtis Huttenhower, Natalia Palacios
pmc-13388000.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We conducted a nested case‐control study within the Nurses’ Health Study and the Health Professionals Follow‐up Study to examine the role of the gut virome (GV) in Parkinson's disease (PD). We applied a novel metagenomic virome profiling approach, Bioinformatic Application for Quantification and Labeling of Viral taxonomy (BAQLaVa), to prospectively collected metagenomic data from 62 participants with PD, 123 healthy controls, and 90 participants with prodromal PD (pPD).

pmc-13400144.title: Ion sequential therapy aligned with pathological changes enhances cardiac function after myocardial infarction
pmc-13400144.creator: Yiming Zhong, Zhaowenbin Zhang, Shixing Huang, Ao Shen, Bei Qian, Qiang Long, Zhaoxi Qi, Xiaojun He, Yecen Zhang, Lan Chang, Wangxi Hai, Xinming Wang, Zhengwei You, Qiang Zhao, Jiang Chang, Xiaofeng Ye

pmc-13576854.title: Multitarget Pharmacological Mechanisms and Safety Profiles of Six Ethnobotanically Prioritized Indonesian Medicinal Plants for Cardiometabolic Disorders: A Systematic Review
pmc-13576854.creator: Febrina A Saputri, Raden M Febriyanti, Zulfan Zazuli, Callista A Mulyadi, Citra Aulia Rahma, Made A N D Putri, Najwa Kirana
pmc-13576854.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This systematic review, conducted per PRISMA guidelines, examined the pharmacological activities and safety of six ethnobotanically prioritized medicinal plants for cardiometabolic disease: Gynura procumbens, Mimosa pudica, Tithonia diversifolia, Leucaena leucocephala, Smallanthus sonchifolius, and Syzygium cumini. Searches of PubMed and Scopus yielded 81 records, of which 66 studies met eligibility criteria, comprising in silico (n = 15), in vitro (n = 43), in vivo/clinical (n = 40), and safety/toxicity (n = 54) evidence.

pmc-13587115.title: Distribution of Big Tau Isoforms in the Human Central and Peripheral Nervous System
pmc-13587115.creator: Rama Krishna Koppisetti, Nicolas R. Barthélemy, Kanta Horie, Cindy V. Ly, Kaleigh F. Roberts, Srinivas Koutarapu, Richard J. Perrin, Erin E. pmc-13587115.description: ObjectiveTau is widely studied in neurodegeneration, yet most work has focused on canonical brain tau isoforms. A longer isoform, “big tau,” produced by inclusion of exon 4a, is expressed in the peripheral nervous system (PNS) and central nervous system (CNS) regions. We sought to characterize big tau composition, anatomic distribution, and disease relevance.
